bull_bear.body: Shift to outcome-based pricing in AI projects (e.g., 50% cost reduction in KYC refresh) rather than pure FTE models; Internal adoption of 'Roboworx/Cogniflows' by 3,000+ employees driving productivity before client billing; Subcon expense spike was purely accounting reclassification, not operational shift.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Dividend of INR 1 proposed for FY27.
- Cash and Cash Equivalents were INR 12,589 mm at Q1 FY27 against INR 12,810 mm at FY26; per share, cash was INR 137 at Q1 FY27 versus current book value per share of INR 300. Note the deck flags that effective Q4FY25 deposits of more than 12 months are included in this figure.
- Current Book Value per share has risen on the deck's series from INR 179 (FY23) to INR 300 (Q1 FY27), with the deck noting historical numbers were changed due to the Bonus issued in Q4 FY26.
- Hedging is a deliberate treasury policy rather than opportunistic: total outstanding hedges of $273.6 mm at an average INR 93.41/$, 100% forwards, laddered out to FY29 Q1 (Total FY27 $156.20 mm at 91.16; Total FY28 $112.00 mm at 96.20; Total FY29 $5.40 mm at 100.85).
- The deck cites a 17.5% 4-Year Revenue CAGR from FY22 to FY26.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- "One eClerx" unification of client-facing, pre-sales and solutioning teams to capture Large Strategic Deals and expand into adjacent domains of strength
- Enterprise AI orchestration platform (Roboworx CogniFlows) with a pre-built agentic workbench and integrations with all leading frontier models
- Foundational partnerships with top hyperscalers and AI platforms including Databricks and Adobe
- Analyst recognition as Leader and Star Performer across two key service offerings and Major Contender status in three others
- Recognized Partner of the Year for a second consecutive year by one of the world's largest telecommunications providers, alongside multiple other partner awards
- Diversified, geographically distributed delivery footprint (India, Manila, Cairo, Lima, London, Singapore) reducing client and geographic concentration risk
- Deep domain expertise combined with agentic AI-enabled service delivery across BFSI, high-tech and telecom verticals
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Client concentration risk — Large clients possess greater bargaining power, which can result in pricing concessions, extended payment terms, or demands for additional scope at no incremental cost, compressing margins over time; deterioration, delayed payments, insolvency, or a change in control/strategy at a top client (e.g. insourcing or vendor consolidation) can lead to abrupt, largely uncontrollable loss of business.
- Currency risk — The Company earned 87% of its revenue in US Dollars, 9% in Euros, and 4% in Sterling and other currencies, so exchange rate fluctuations can negatively impact financial performance; hedging strategies are used but do not eliminate the exposure.
- Competition risk — The industry is highly competitive and evolving rapidly, with changing client expectations, new entrants, technology disruption and pricing pressure; low barriers to entry in certain segments allow well-funded technology-first players to disrupt traditional service models, particularly areas susceptible to automation or platform-based delivery.
- Legal and regulatory risk — Legislation in some client countries may restrict outsourcing of work to overseas entities like eClerx, which could hamper growth in major markets; withdrawal or material alteration of export/tax incentives, and evolving regulation around AI, cybersecurity, sanctions, employment and data protection, could increase compliance obligations, operational complexity and costs.
- Technological / AI disruption risk — Rapid advances in automation, AI and digital tools are reshaping client expectations and service delivery models; competitors that adopt new technologies faster, or clients that build in-house automation, could reduce demand for traditional service offerings and erode eClerx's competitive positioning if it does not keep pace with innovation.
- Cyber security incident / cyber attack risk — The business relies extensively on IT systems and handles significant volumes of confidential client data; a breach (hacking, phishing, malware, insider threat, ransomware or DoS attack) could cause unauthorized data access/theft, breach client confidentiality agreements, trigger regulatory penalties and SLA/contractual liability, and reliance on third-party vendors/cloud providers adds exposure outside direct control.
- Key people risk — The business is critically dependent on the quality, expertise and commitment of its workforce; inability to attract, develop, retain and motivate key talent could adversely affect service delivery quality, client expectations and long-term growth objectives.
- Integration risk from acquisitions — Past or future acquisitions may pose financial, technological, operational and people integration risks; challenges integrating acquired businesses, personnel, technology platforms, internal controls and organizational cultures could divert management attention, disrupt ongoing business, increase costs, and expose the Company to cyber and information security risks.

business.body:
- Described as "a global leader in AI-powered analytics, digital operations, automation, and business process management", partnering with Fortune 500 enterprises across financial services, telecom, media & entertainment, luxury, retail & fashion, and manufacturing.
- Delivery footprint spans 17 countries with around 22,500 employees, serving clients across the Americas, APAC and EMEA from global delivery centres.
- Client base is broad rather than concentrated in one vertical: Q1'FY27 revenue by industry is BFSI 37.6%, CMT 26.2%, HiTech and M&D 16.3%, Fashion & Luxury and Retail 8.2%, Emerging 11.7%.
- Top 10 client contribution was 60% in FY27 Q1, versus 63% in FY26 Q1 and 62% in FY25 Q1 — i.e. gradually declining concentration on the deck's own series.
- Geographic concentration in FY27 Q1: North America 78%, Europe 16%, ROW 6%; currency contribution USD 87%, EURO 8%, GBP 3%, Others 2%.

outlook.body: Q4 new wins USD 46M; Analytics/Automation book at USD 90M; Strong pipeline in KYC, financial crime, and Agentic AI deployments starting Q1FY27.

outlook.body: Agentic AI scaling across verticals; Market360 expansion into Fortune 1000 retail/CPG; FCC services outside financial services; Geographic diversification (Manila, Cairo).
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Reorienting the BFSI business around data and AI, with targeted investment in client-facing field teams, leadership, India-based technology and AI capabilities, product development, and employee enablement
- Financial Crime and Compliance retained as a key area of strategic focus, with continued investment in solutioning, product capabilities and AI-enabled functionality
- In Trade Lifecycle, actively applying AI-driven ideas from the existing book of work to improve productivity, enhance controls and create new opportunities with existing clients and new logos
- High-Tech, Manufacturing and Distribution, Fashion & Luxury, Retail and Consumer Goods: focus on identifying and expanding strategic accounts, driving cross-sell across the broader capability portfolio, accelerating new client acquisition in Marketing Intelligence and Data Operations, expanding Digital Marketing offerings, and enhancing Finance and Accounting capabilities
- Cable, Media and Telecommunications: client growth and diversification central to strategy, expanding into new industries and geographic markets while increasing share of wallet within existing accounts through cross-selling and integrated solution offerings
- Following the successful launch of Network Operations Center (NOC) capabilities, continuing to invest in technology-led operational services (infrastructure support and adjacent technical operations) to broaden the portfolio beyond traditional customer operations
- AI positioned as a key strategic growth driver across Customer Operations, embedding intelligent automation, predictive analytics, conversational AI and real-time decision support into service delivery
- Continued investment in the global delivery network, further strengthening strategic delivery locations such as Manila, Cairo and Lima
- Continuously strengthening perimeter and internal security infrastructure (IAM rollout, PAM, SIEM, email security) to scale in step with the growing hybrid workforce
- eClerx maintains a formal Dividend Distribution Policy under Regulation 43A of the Listing Regulations, considering financial parameters and internal/external factors when deciding between distribution and retention of profits; the Board's stated intent is to maintain its historical dividend payout ratio, exploring efficient methods to do so. During the year, the Company also returned surplus funds to shareholders via a share buyback, with the bought-back shares extinguished and paid-up capital reduced accordingly. Profit for the year was retained by carrying it forward to Retained Earnings rather than transferring it to General Reserve.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: eClerx continued to expand its global delivery footprint during FY26. In BFSI, it established a new team in Lima, Peru and grew its onshore teams in Singapore and London, while its Fayetteville Center of Excellence for Financial Crime and Compliance continued to scale, adding new clients and broadening client/functional diversification. In Cable, Media and Telecommunications, it continued to expand delivery capabilities in Manila, Cairo and Lima to support scalable, multilingual, digitally enabled customer operations; the Cairo site, within its first year of operations, became the top-performing site in the region for a global client. The company also launched advanced Network Operations Center (NOC) services for one of the world's largest global infrastructure companies. In the Emerging vertical, an additional floor was taken up in Manila to support strong growth in Finance and Accounting services. In Fashion & Luxury, new studio offerings were launched in Paris and Milan alongside AI-enabled creative services. On the technology side, eClerx launched Roboworx CogniFlows, its Enterprise AI orchestration platform with a pre-built agentic workbench, and established foundational partnerships with hyperscalers/AI platforms including Databricks and Adobe.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- AI has become a central topic across client conversations, as organizations evaluate how to apply new technologies to improve productivity, strengthen controls, and accelerate transformation
- Demand for intelligent automation, data-driven insights, and scalable digital operations continues to grow across verticals
- The pace of client decision-making may be affected as clients refine their own AI roadmaps, a potential near-term headwind
- Integrated technology-and-analytics model combined with embedded AI-enabled capabilities continues to resonate with clients and strengthens differentiated market positioning
- Continued momentum in Finance & Accounting/FAO services within the Emerging vertical is expected to carry forward into FY27
- Growth in QA360 (AI-powered Quality Intelligence platform) driven by shift from traditional interaction sampling to continuous, intelligence-driven performance optimisation
- BFSI: healthy pipeline supporting entry into the new year, plus a growing pipeline in Financial Crime and Compliance
- High-Tech, Manufacturing and Distribution, Fashion & Luxury, Retail and Consumer Goods: robust pipeline of strategic opportunities and growing market traction, plus a strong pipeline of large strategic deals
- Emerging vertical: pipeline continues to be robust, reflecting sustained client demand for digital services, especially FAO services
- QA360: multiple new client deployments planned
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: eClerx delivered record FY26 results with 17.9% USD revenue growth and 132 bps margin expansion, driven by a $90M analytics book and first large-scale Agentic AI wins, positioning it for top-quartile growth in FY27 despite macro headwinds. The strategic pivot to outcome-based AI services and diversification beyond BFSI reduces concentration risk while enhancing operating leverage.
